description: Sector-agnostic, declarative specification of what a company record must contain and how its completeness is measured, gated and sourced. This is a contract/schema artifact only — it defines no scoring code and populates no company data; see docs/architecture/data-factory-18-categories.md for the full rationale and docs/factory/README (inline below) for how sector packs extend it.
overall_threshold_rationale: 95% overall, matching this project's own existing language in docs/data/telecom-sector.md ('the 18-category 95% target') and docs/DATA_MODEL_18_CATEGORIES.md/docs/MASTER_SCHEMA.md. The overall figure is a weighted average of the 18 category scores using each category's weight below, but it is gated: overall readiness additionally requires every category's own hard_gates to pass and every category's own completeness_threshold to be met — a high weighted average cannot substitute for a failing category, per the anti-averaging principle.
anti_averaging_principle: A category's hard_gates are pass/fail conditions that cannot be offset by strength elsewhere. The overall weighted score is informative, but a data factory run is only 'ready' when (a) the weighted average >= overall_completeness_threshold, (b) every category's own score >= its own completeness_threshold, and (c) every category's hard_gates all pass. This mirrors language already in this branch's docs/data/telecom-sector.md: 'the engine must not label the sector ready before the weighted score and all hard gates pass.'

applicability.description: Every company has an identity, a governance structure and an industry context. No sector pack may mark this category not_applicable in whole; only individual fields within it (e.g. sharia_status for a non-Saudi cross-listed issuer) may be narrowed by a sector/company pack flag.

unavailable_conditions.rule: A field may only be marked unavailable after an official_source_type listed for this category has actually been checked (a retrieval was attempted, not skipped) and the reason is one of allowed_reasons. A bare unavailable flag with no evidence_fields populated is invalid and must be rejected by the same validator that rejects a missing required field.

not_applicable_conditions.rule: not_applicable is a structural, sector/company-pack-driven determination (see applicability), never an extraction outcome. It must cite the flag or rule that made it inapplicable, not silence.

categories.threshold_rationale: Default 85% floor. Identity fields (company_model) are near-100% obtainable from the registry and audited statements, but governance_profile narrative fields (board bios, committee charters) are frequently only partially disclosed even by well-governed issuers, so a 95% floor here would make the category chronically unmeetable rather than diagnostic.

hard_gates.condition: company_model completeness < 60%
hard_gates.action: category is treated as failing regardless of governance_profile/industry_context scores; a company record cannot be usable without a minimally identified issuer

applicability.description: Relative valuation multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA, etc.) are internally computed and always applicable. Consensus-estimate fields require the company to actually have third-party coverage; absence of coverage is a structural fact about the company, not a missing extraction.

categories.threshold_rationale: 80%, below the default, and explicitly justified per docs/MASTER_SCHEMA.md's own valuation gap notes: the DCF-style intrinsic fields need an issuer/analyst WACC and terminal-growth assumption this project does not fabricate, and the consensus field_group needs licensed or attributed third-party data this project does not yet purchase (see project_data_source_decision memory: no paid data API until revenue). categories.source_cost_notes: Relative multiples computed internally are free. notes: extraction_mode is requires_review at the category level because materiality tagging (dividend_flag, earnings_flag, governance_flag, etc.) and Arabic/English title reconciliation are judgment calls; the announcement's existence, date and source_url are deterministic, but its classification is not auto-published without review. If an LLM-assisted reader proposes the classification, that proposal is still requires_review — it is never treated as itself an official_source_type (see FORBIDDEN_SOURCE_TYPES in this contract's build script / the 'no LLM as source' hard rule).

Kept below the 95% statement floor because operational KPIs are voluntarily disclosed rather than statutorily audited — this project's own telecom work already documents real, permanent gaps here (e.g. 'stc does not publish ARPU in the reviewed 2021-2025 reports and no proxy is invented', docs/data/telecom-sector.md) that no amount of collection effort closes.

categories.source_cost_notes: Every operational KPI on this project has come from the issuer's own presentations/transcripts; none has required a paid vendor.

freshness_policy.refresh_trigger: issuer's next quarterly results deck/call, same cadence family as financial_statements

notes: extraction_mode is requires_review at the category level because operational KPI disclosures are frequently ambiguous in scope (e.g. the Mobily 5G/'99% coverage' figures documented in telecom-sector.md as deliberately not extracted because the metric's basis was unclear) — a reviewer must confirm the metric's definition matches the catalog field before publish, it is never auto-accepted from a structured table alone the way an audited statement line is.

applicability.condition: a company is assigned exactly the sector-specific financial-statement-shaped field_groups its sector pack activates (e.g. banking for a bank); this is the category the task description's 'Banking-Specific' example maps to
applicability.description: Holds sector-specific balance-sheet/income/ratio lines that replace or supplement the universal financial_statements/profitability categories for a given sector (gross_loans, net_interest_margin for banks; loss_ratio, combined_ratio for insurers; FFO/NAV for REITs) — distinct from category 15's physical operating-unit KPIs.

unavailable_conditions.rule: A field may only be marked unavailable after an official_source_type listed for this category has actually been checked (a retrieval was attempted, not skipped) and the reason is one of allowed_reasons. A bare unavailable flag with no evidence_fields populated is invalid and must be rejected by the same validator that rejects a missing required field.

not_applicable_conditions.rule: not_applicable is a structural, sector/company-pack-driven determination (see applicability), never an extraction outcome. It must cite the flag or rule that made it inapplicable, not silence.

categories.threshold_rationale: 90%, matching the task description's own worked example ('Banking-Specific >=90%'). Set below the universal 95% financial_statements floor because sector-specific templates (Basel III KM1 rows, IFRS 17 insurance disclosures) are newer reporting requirements some issuers are still phasing in, a real transitional gap distinct from ordinary statement completeness.

hard_gates.condition: sector_pack activates this category for a company and its score is materially near zero while financial_statements and profitability both pass their own thresholds
hard_gates.action: overall readiness cannot be labeled ready; this is the contract's direct implementation of the anti-averaging principle named in the task ('a whole category cannot be near-zero even if others are strong'), and mirrors the existing project rule in docs/data/telecom-sector.md that 'the engine must not label the sector ready before the weighted score and all hard gates pass'

categories.source_cost_notes: Sector-specific statement lines and ratios are computed/extracted from the same audited statements and regulator templates as financial_statements; no paid feed required.

freshness_policy.refresh_trigger: issuer files its next quarterly/annual statement (same cadence as financial_statements)

applicability.condition: applicable whenever the underlying financial_statements/market_data inputs a given metric needs are themselves populated; a metric needing a longer history than the company has listed (e.g. a 10-year CAGR) is not_applicable for that company, not unavailable
applicability.description: Composite/smart scores (Piotroski F-score, Altman Z-score, Beneish M-score, accrual ratio) and long-window analytics (10y CAGRs, total returns, moving averages). All are internally computed, never fetched.

unavailable_conditions.rule: A field may only be marked unavailable after an official_source_type listed for this category has actually been checked (a retrieval was attempted, not skipped) and the reason is one of allowed_reasons. A bare unavailable flag with no evidence_fields populated is invalid and must be rejected by the same validator that rejects a missing required field.

not_applicable_conditions.rule: not_applicable is a structural, sector/company-pack-driven determination (see applicability), never an extraction outcome. It must cite the flag or rule that made it inapplicable, not silence.

categories.threshold_rationale: 90%. As pure derivations over already-required inputs, these should compute almost completely once financial_statements/market_data are in place; kept just under 95% only because several fields (10-year CAGRs, 200-day moving averages) need a longer listing history than some companies in the universe have had, by construction.

hard_gates.condition: a composite score (piotroski_f_score, altman_z_score, beneish_m_score) is populated while one of its declared component sub-scores is marked unavailable
hard_gates.action: rejected; a composite score can never be computed from a partial input set with the gap silently zero-filled — it must be marked missing_formula_inputs_or_history as a whole instead

categories.source_cost_notes: Entirely internal computation over already-sourced data; never requires a paid feed.

provenance_requirements.calculated_field_supplement: Every field in this category must carry a formula_id and its full list of consumed input field_key/period pairs — this is the category where 'no AI/LLM as a source' matters most operationally, since a formula_id must resolve to a declared, versioned, human-authored formula in the codebase, never to an LLM-estimated number.

freshness_policy.refresh_trigger: recomputed whenever any input it depends on changes value

applicability.condition: applies to every fact in every other category; this category's own score is not measured over a distinct field list but over the provenance completeness of all other categories' populated facts
applicability.description: Not a content category like 1-17. It is the audit layer: for every fact published anywhere in the contract, did it carry the provenance_requirements its own category mandates, and is it within its own category's freshness_policy. This category exists so provenance/freshness is scored and gated explicitly rather than assumed.

unavailable_conditions.rule: A field may only be marked unavailable after an official_source_type listed for this category has actually been checked (a retrieval was attempted, not skipped) and the reason is one of allowed_reasons. A bare unavailable flag with no evidence_fields populated is invalid and must be rejected by the same validator that rejects a missing required field.

not_applicable_conditions.determined_by: n/a — this category has no not_applicable path; every published fact everywhere must carry lineage
not_applicable_conditions.rule: not_applicable is a structural, sector/company-pack-driven determination (see applicability), never an extraction outcome. It must cite the flag or rule that made it inapplicable, not silence.

categories.threshold_rationale: 100%, matching the task description's own worked example ('Sources/Lineage/Freshness=100%'). Unlike every other category, an incomplete provenance record is not a disclosure gap to tolerate — it means a fact should not have been published at all, so there is no principled floor below 100% here; a fact failing this check is pulled from the numerator of whatever category it belongs to, not merely flagged.

hard_gates.condition: any published fact anywhere in the dataset is missing one of its own category's provenance_requirements.mandatory_fields
hard_gates.action: that fact is excluded from its category's completeness numerator entirely (it does not count as populated) until the missing provenance is supplied — this is the single hard gate that enforces every other category's provenance_requirements block

hard_gates.condition: any published fact's age exceeds its own category's freshness_policy.max_age_before_stale_days
hard_gates.action: the fact is flagged stale and excluded from the 'currently fresh' completeness numerator, even though it remains visible as historical data with its staleness disclosed

categories.source_cost_notes: This category is metadata about other facts' sourcing, not itself sourced data; it has no direct cost.

freshness_policy.refresh_trigger: continuous audit re-run on every publish
